idea-plugin.name: Handoff for Claude Code
idea-plugin.description:
Handoff is the place where Claude Code hands work over to you, and you hand the result back.

Some steps an AI agent should not run on its own: deploys, logins, releases, uploads. Instead of copying a command out of the chat, running it somewhere and pasting the output back, Claude proposes it through the IDE's MCP server. It shows up in the Handoff tool window with the reason and the working directory. Run it, edit it first or dismiss it; exit code and output go straight back to Claude.

Features

  • Proposed commands with reason and working directory, risky ones (deploy, push, publish, delete) highlighted.
  • One click to run, output in the Run tool window. Edit the command before running, or dismiss it with a note for Claude.
  • Result back to Claude: exit code and the last lines of output, no copy and paste.
  • One changelist per task: files Claude changes for a task land in their own changelist "Claude: <task>", ready to review and commit on their own. Several sessions in one project each keep their own task.
  • Review with line notes: Claude asks you to review its changes; open the diff, attach notes to single lines (hover a line, click the +) and approve or send the notes back, each with path, line and code.
  • Command sequences: several commands as one card, run all or step by step, stops at the first failure. Copy on every command card if you would rather run it yourself.
  • Claude is waiting (optional): a card and a notification when a Claude Code session in the project is done or needs your input. Read the full message in an editor tab and type your next prompt right into the card.
  • Claude sessions in editor tabs: start Claude Code from the IDE and work with it in an editor tab, the conversation formatted, prompts and slash commands sent to the terminal in the background. /show-in-editor opens a running session there, Open in Handoff in the terminal's menu shows the session of that tab, and ↶ next to a prompt rewinds to before it. Copy code blocks and messages; the globe runs Remote Control.
  • Sessions: all Claude Code sessions of the project at a glance, with state, model, context use and running task, one click to their tab or terminal.
  • Session logs (.jsonl): Claude Code's transcripts open as a readable conversation instead of raw JSON (switch to Text at the bottom), with tool steps, errors and changed files; resume one in a new tab or export it as Markdown.
  • Questions with options: Claude asks as a card, one answer or several, plus your own answer.
  • Checklists for manual tests: the steps to try by hand as a card, each with a checkbox and a note; the results go back to Claude in one go.
  • Secrets: type a password or token into a card; Handoff writes it into the file (e.g. .env) and Claude never sees it.
  • Notifications when something is waiting while the IDE is in the background.
  • Images to review or choose from: one image to approve, or several variants to pick one. A viewer with zoom and paging lets you mark areas with a frame and a note for Claude, or draw on the image with a pen or arrows.
  • Memory: everything Claude Code loads into each session (CLAUDE.md files, imports, project memory) as a tree with token estimates per file and section, warnings for memories missing from the index, on-demand files and duplicated paragraphs.
  • Usage: tokens per day and session for the project, and optionally your 5-hour and weekly plan limits.
  • Nothing runs without your click.

Setup

  • Enable the IDE's MCP server (Settings | Tools | MCP Server) and connect Claude Code to it.
  • Claude Code then sees the tools handoff_propose_command, handoff_propose_sequence, handoff_wait_for_result, handoff_show_images, handoff_ask, handoff_checklist, handoff_request_secret, handoff_request_review, handoff_get_notes, handoff_begin_task and handoff_end_task.
  • Tell Claude when to use them: the empty Commands tab copies a ready-made snippet for your CLAUDE.md.
  • The built-in guide (Guide in the tool window's ⋮ menu) lists the setup and a prompt per feature.

Works with Claude Code and other MCP clients. Not affiliated with Anthropic.

You can support it via GitHub Sponsors or buy me a coffee on Ko-fi.
